skill.name: remotion-studio
skill.description: Start Remotion Studio, obtain its local URL, and preview the current video project in a browser.
skill.summary: Launch Remotion Studio for browser-based video previews.
skill.author: remotion-dev

security_audit.summary: All four static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fence or inline-code delimiters. The documented command intentionally starts Remotion Studio with fixed arguments, and no command injection or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: | `--port=<number>` | Request a Studio server port; otherwise Remotion finds a free port.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 9 through 11 are a fenced Bash example containing a fixed Remotion CLI command. The backticks delimit Markdown and do not perform Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 11 is the closing delimiter of a Markdown code fence. It is documentation syntax, not an executable backtick expression.
Line 22 uses inline Markdown backticks to format a command option and its accepted log levels. No shell or Ruby execution occurs in this table row.
Line 23 uses inline Markdown backticks to format the port option. The text documents a numeric argument and contains no executable backtick expression.

content.value_statement: Starting a local Remotion preview and locating its browser URL can interrupt development. This skill launches Studio and guides you to the active preview.
actual_capabilities: Starts Remotion Studio without automatically opening a browser.
Reports the URL for an existing Studio instance.
Keeps a new Studio process running when no instance exists.
Supports error, warning, information, and verbose log levels.
Supports requesting a specific Studio server port.
Supports starting another instance with the force-new option.
limitations: It previews the current project but does not render or export a final video.
It does not install dependencies or create a Remotion project.
A browser is required to use the printed Studio URL.
A new Studio instance can remain active as a long-running process.

use_cases.title: Preview a Composition
use_cases.description: Launch Studio and open the local URL while developing a Remotion composition.

use_cases.title: Review Motion Changes
use_cases.description: Start a browser preview for checking animation, timing, and visual updates.

use_cases.title: Inspect Local Projects
use_cases.description: Request a known port and use detailed logs while reviewing a team project.

output_examples.output: Starts Remotion Studio without opening a browser automatically, then provides the local Studio URL.

output_examples.input: Open Studio on my preferred port with detailed logs.
output_examples.output: Requests the selected port, enables verbose logging, and reports the available preview URL.

output_examples.input: Start another Studio instance for comparison.
output_examples.output: Forces a separate Studio process to start and provides its browser URL.

best_practices: Run the skill from the intended Remotion project directory.
Use a specific port when other local tools depend on a stable address.
Stop long-running Studio processes after completing the preview session.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a substitute for rendering or exporting video.
Do not force new instances when the existing Studio URL is sufficient.
Do not expose the local Studio server to untrusted networks.

faq.question: What does this skill start?
faq.answer: It starts Remotion Studio for the current project and reports the local preview URL.

faq.question: Does it open the browser automatically?
faq.answer: The Studio command disables automatic browser opening. The workflow then opens the reported URL.

faq.question: What happens when Studio is already running?
faq.answer: The existing Studio URL is printed, and the new command exits.

faq.question: Can I choose the server port?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a port number, or let Remotion select an available port.

faq.question: Which log levels are available?
faq.answer: The documented levels are error, warning, information, and verbose. Information is the default.

faq.question: Can it start multiple Studio instances?
faq.answer: Yes. The force-new option starts another instance for the same project and port.
